newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rebels ready to resume stalled peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rebels ready to resume stalled peace talks.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-10-02

text.p: Mexico's Zapatista rebels on Wednesday said they were ready to return to the negotiating table to revive stalled peace talks, and challenged the government to do likewise.

"We challenge the government, to demonstrate the same disposition (to reach an agreement) with facts," a communique signed by rebel leader Subcommander Marcos said. It was released in this colonial city in southern Chiapas state.

Zapatistas rose up in arms against the government on Jan. 1, 1994, demanding land and greater indigenous rights in Chiapas. At least 145 people were killed in the initial fighting until cease-fires were declared, although since then there has been little bloodshed.
Long-winded peace talks have produced few results so far.
The Zapatistas walked out of the latest round on Sept. 3, charging the government of not being serious after President Ernesto Zedillo said they were "good guerrillas."
"If the federal government has, as it says it has, a legitimate desire to resolve this conflict through dialogue, it must show it," the rebel communique said.

A second communique, also signed by Marcos, dismissed a government warning to Zapatistas not to attend an indigenous congress in the Mexican capital next week with the ironic headline "UUY," denoting fear in Spanish.

The government this week warned Zapatista rebels not to leave their stronghold in the southern state of Chiapas until peace accords were signed. It has been said that they risked arrest if they left the state to attend the meeting.
Marcos noted in the communique that the government had been trying to kill the rebels since their uprising, but did not say whether they would attend the congress.
